## 0.6.2 (2026-10-30)


### Release Highlights

**🚀 LoopTroop — What's New Since v0.6.1**

A major update bringing a new AI assistant, smarter error recovery, and more reliable ticket execution!

- **1. 💬 Meet Your New AI Chat Assistant!** — Talk to AI directly inside LoopTroop! Ask how LoopTroop works, get help understanding features, or ask questions about your tickets, their progress, errors, and history.
- **2. 🎯 AI That Understands Your Tickets** — The assistant uses real ticket logs, planning documents, project code, and documentation to answer questions with supporting references. Chat about one specific ticket or across all your attached projects.
- **3. 🗂️ Multiple Chats & Conversation History** — Keep several AI conversations open, switch between them, search previous chats, rename conversations, and copy messages. Saved conversations can be reopened later!
- **4. 🧠 Choose Your AI & See Its Thinking** — Configure a separate AI model for chatting, select its reasoning effort, and see live responses. When supported by the model, you can expand its thinking process.
- **5. 🔄 Smarter Retry & Continue** — Failed AI tasks are easier to recover. Retry starts a fresh AI session, while Continue resumes the previous conversation when possible, preserving completed work.
- **6. ✍️ Tell the AI How to Retry** — Add custom instructions when retrying a failed task or individual AI council member. Guide the AI toward a solution without restarting the entire workflow.
- **7. 📂 Work With Files Outside Your Repository** — Tickets can now target files in external folders, with visible warnings when work extends beyond the repository.
- **8. ✅ Tickets Without Code Changes** — Tasks involving only checks or external files can now finish successfully without creating unnecessary Git commits or pull requests.
- **9. 🛡️ Safer AI Code Delivery** — Stronger safeguards help prevent AI agents from directly modifying protected project files or pushing changes to GitHub. LoopTroop remains responsible for delivering code.
- **10. 🔀 Better Recovery From Early PR Merges** — If a pull request gets merged before LoopTroop finishes, it can verify what was merged and prepare a separate corrective PR for any remaining changes.
- **✨ Overall:** LoopTroop is becoming easier to use and more reliable, with a major new way to interact with your projects: **just ask the AI!**

### Summary

- Package installs now require Node.js 24.18.1 or newer, which includes the July security fixes.
- The development frontend opens through Tailscale Serve (`*.ts.net`) instead of answering "Blocked request".
- Read LoopTroop docs, source, and ticket evidence in one read-only assistant, with shared scoped tabs, copyable messages, and model-provided reasoning.
- Clear deleted ticket chats from open tabs on view changes, and keep newer answers after close failures.
- Beads support external file targets with visible warnings and explicit empty targets; tickets with no repository changes finish without an empty commit or PR.
- Retry starts failed AI work in a fresh session, with optional user guidance across supported AI steps; Continue preserves the existing conversation.
- Model-generated YAML values beginning with `,`, `]`, or `}` now parse without changing their text.
- AI workflow prompts receive shared delivery guidance, while the request guard refuses direct GitHub and remote Git writes.
- LoopTroop verifies early-merged ticket PRs and safely returns remaining work through review.

### Added

- Add a shared read-only assistant window on the dashboard and inside tickets, with citations and notices for missing evidence.
- Copy individual user and assistant messages using small text controls, rename conversations, or copy a conversation's messages from its tab menu. Conversation copies omit reasoning.
- Show model-provided reasoning live in a collapsed section with available model and effort details. Filter recognizable credentials and display a short unavailable message when the provider supplies none.
- Configure the assistant model separately below the council settings, with the existing model, effort, and routing controls. Save chat sessions is enabled by default and applies to new conversations. Closing a conversation archives it when saving is enabled or deletes its OpenCode session otherwise; hiding the window preserves open conversations. Search saved history by title and scope, then restore a conversation without changing the current screen.
- Keep assistant conversations separate from workflow sessions and deny editing, shell commands, workflow actions, and reads outside prepared evidence. Repository snapshots keep ordinary source filenames and skip private paths, generated files, and symbolic links inside the project. Ticket logs and artifacts are redacted, collected within limits, and marked incomplete when history or a project is unavailable. Archived conversations remain available while OpenCode retains their sessions.
- Preserve drafts, open tabs, and running replies when switching between dashboard and ticket context. A blank chat creates its conversation on the first send. Keep citations in a separate browser tab, follow replies while the reader is at the bottom, and offer a jump control when they scroll up. Unchanged assistant model settings can be saved while model discovery is unavailable.
- Remove ticket-scoped conversations when their ticket or project is deleted or reset. Keep dashboard history, including past replies from legacy Help conversations and replies about deleted tickets, and refresh dashboard evidence for later questions. Damaged conversation records cannot interrupt valid history; failed remote deletion keeps a receipt for retry. A conversation is refused if its ticket disappears while it is being created.

### Changed

- Use one assistant experience for documentation, LoopTroop source, and ticket evidence. Dashboard conversations cover every attached project and ticket regardless of board filters; conversations started in a ticket view use only that ticket and its project. Keep open tabs shared across dashboard and ticket views while each conversation retains its creation scope. Selecting an open tab or history entry leaves the current screen in place, and a new chat uses the dashboard or ticket currently shown. Tint the full ticket tab with its project's color. Sending the first message creates the first conversation, after which **New chat** appears. Legacy Help conversations become dashboard-scoped, while existing ticket conversations stay bound to their ticket.
- Open the assistant window against the bottom and right edges, covering the launcher while open, and allow it to move by dragging; remember its position for the current browser session. Keep the inverted-color launcher in the same fixed bottom-right position across views, at 70% opacity at rest and 100% on hover.

### Fixed

- Use formula-scoped, disposable trust for Homebrew audits when the installed Homebrew supports it.
- `npm run dev` and `vite preview` now accept `*.ts.net` host names, so Tailscale Serve can front the loopback Vite server as the documentation describes. Vite's host check had been rejecting those names with a 403. The check stays on: other names are still refused, and another proxy's name can be added through Vite's own `__VITE_ADDITIONAL_SERVER_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, which `vite preview` now inherits.
- Refresh assistant sessions when the ticket view changes so deleted ticket chats are evicted without disturbing other tabs. Cancel a pending close-failure transcript refresh when a new message starts.
- Keep toast notifications visible above the assistant window while it is open.
- Show the assistant conversation menu above the chat window, group model steps into one thinking section per answer, distinguish context preparation from the model response, and retain matching reasoning received during a reply when OpenCode omits it from the returned message.

- Keep retry-note history when ordinary Retry retires guidance or Manual QA recovery succeeds. Preserve council guidance notices through Continue and refinement, discard saved Full Answers when a model is stopped or Part 1 is restarted, and keep phase retry notes on the failed PRD part, including workflow timeouts. Recheck coding recovery ownership before reset, cleanup, and bead updates. Recover aged interview stop reservations without bypassing remote-stop confirmation, and block owned unexpected interview request failures while preserving submitted answers. Hold interview ownership through terminal route handling so stale failures cannot block identical successor submissions.

- Accept external bead targets on Windows, macOS, Linux, and WSL, and explicit empty target lists without inventing repository files. Missing or malformed target lists remain invalid. Existing single-path normalization shows the affected bead and its before/after correction. Approval and execution flag absolute or repository-escaping target paths, including relative symbolic-link escapes resolved on the server. Runtime bead payloads carry their targets and derived warnings before the full tracker loads. Reject control characters and line separators in individual target paths; planning models may read external folders before bead approval, while read-only phases still prohibit edits. External access has no folder allowlist, separate permission step, or automatic backup and remains subject to operating-system permissions and existing managed-state protections. External changes are outside Git recovery.
- Complete checks-only and external-only tickets after normal testing, configured Manual QA, and cleanup when integration proves there are no repository changes. Record `noRepositoryChanges` in the integration report without creating an empty commit, pushing a candidate, or opening a PR. Real Git failures still block.
- Stop and abandon failed AI sessions before manual Retry, including Retry with extra note, so refinement and coverage cannot reconnect to the stuck conversation. Preserve completed planning, saved interview answers, coding checkpoints, and successful-code finalization recovery. Interrupt failed turns even when preserving their conversations for Continue, and confirm the stop before sending another prompt. If the stop cannot be confirmed, keep the ticket blocked. Interview batch timeouts preserve submitted answers, and Continue resumes cached interview sessions at the failed step. Pull-request drafting Continue reuses its saved file audit only while the base and candidate still match; otherwise it requires a fresh Retry.
- Make workspace setup retry notes use a fresh session, matching other AI retries. Support extra notes for failed AI steps and individual council-member restarts. Notes are passed unchanged to the affected work and retained in its history without changing approved documents or other members' results. Stop applying the note after that work succeeds so later batches, coverage passes, and phase runs do not inherit it. Manual QA replays failed submissions only after explicit recovery and does not reuse AI candidates generated under different retry guidance. Drafts steered by member retry notes carry the same anonymous operator-guidance notice as drafts steered by answered AI questions; Continue keeps its existing same-session behavior.
- Keep Retry and Continue tied to the current blocked error while confirming remote stops. Recover pending interview stops without allowing overlapping requests, preserve the recovery claim through dispatch, and report lost ownership as a conflict. Clear pending continuation requests when their sessions are retired. Preserve initial setup-plan and final-test conversations after eligible AI failures. Carry preserved-session diagnostics through setup reports and council quorum errors, keep workflow attempt ownership separate from automatic retry iterations, and let eligible setup Continue resume after the automatic budget is exhausted. Recover completed Manual QA summaries after interruption without replaying canceled submissions.
- Match pull-request continuation audits against Git's exact filename records, including renames and Unicode names. Require unchanged saved Full Answers before offering PRD Part 2 continuation, retain operator-guidance attribution, and scope member notes to the restarted part.
- Validate target-file entries when saving beads, preserve server-resolved warnings in approval and Coding, and detect symbolic-link traversal without changing native filenames. Missing worktrees keep spelling-based warnings. Refuse no-change completion when uncommitted tracked edits remain.
- Keep Manual QA fix-bead inspection read-only while allowing focused checks of relevant files outside the ticket worktree. Preserve OpenCode/provider diagnostics and session IDs from generation failures so Continue remains available when that session is eligible.
- Quoted model-generated YAML scalars beginning with `,`, `]`, or `}` so stricter `js-yaml` parsing preserves their emitted values.
- Before pushing a candidate, LoopTroop checks for a matching merged PR, verifies its landed commit on the current remote base, fetches the exact PR head, and compares tree proofs. A matching candidate completes from the original PR and stores the original PR, candidate SHA, and proofs. When the candidate has additional changes, LoopTroop applies only those changes to a recovery worktree on the verified base and reruns final tests, optional Manual QA, integration, and PR creation on a separate branch, leaving the merged PR and its branch untouched.
- Recovery keeps corrective PR lineage across repeated early merges, recognizes a candidate delta already present on the base, retries temporary remote failures, checks every matching PR page, normalizes recovery checkout paths across platforms, and preserves manual recovery edits. A committed manual resolution can be adopted on retry; if the base advanced, it is refreshed on the latest verified base and revalidated. A manual resolution with no remaining changes completes from the verified merge; if no correction or recovery checkout survives, retry restarts from the original candidate. Verified merge history remains sufficient after later edits or reverts; local files blocking a clean correction receive their own diagnostic.
- Missing merge proof or a corrective patch conflict preserves the original candidate and any recovery worktree, records manual-recovery details including conflict paths when present, and blocks for resolution. A manual conflict can be resolved in the recovery checkout, committed directly on its recorded base, and retried; LoopTroop adopts it only after confirming the clean commit and reruns final validation.
- OpenCode v2 helper-session discovery stops at the configured session limit instead of following an unbounded child chain.
- Revalidated corrections retain their latest approved content and completion identity after integration creates a new squash commit, including when the base advances before review. Retries reuse saved commit refs and preserve committed manual resolutions if the base advances again.

### Security

- Raise the package floor to Node.js 24.18.1, which includes the July security fixes. The package engine, launcher, installer scripts, and README now use the same floor.
- Preserve structured credential redaction for JSON source files renamed in evidence snapshots, and redact credentials in escaped serialized strings and unquoted values containing punctuation or base64 padding.
- Apply evidence-only assistant permissions when creating sessions and sending questions, and refuse OpenCode updates that do not confirm them. Exclude ignored files, environment and key files, and generated ticket state from repository snapshots. Redact recognizable credentials and signed URL parameters in copied evidence and returned transcripts. Store copied agent instruction files under neutral names and prevent assistant transcripts from being cached by browsers or proxies.
- Nested shell checks follow wrapper directory changes. Tar checks recognize abbreviated options and exact flag precedence, keep option values separate from flags, verify every archive output and extraction directory, and refuse external command helpers and indirect options whose effects cannot be verified. Exclusion-only Git pathspecs receive whole-checkout protection, and inline shell options cannot hide the command behind option values or `--`. Windows filesystem paths retain their separators during command checks. POSIX escapes, including escaped option punctuation, are checked by the shell lexer so escaped quotes and comment apostrophes cannot hide Git or GitHub writes.
- The command guard checks conditional and grouped shell state before trusting the current directory, protects managed Git indexes and stash restoration, checks executable-path, Git helper-path, and loader changes, and preserves BOM-prefixed paths in overwrite checks. It also inspects `watch` and `Start-Process` commands, rejects uninspected interactive shells, and no longer treats ordinary archive or file-mutation operands as help or dry-run flags. Interpreter inline evaluation such as `python -c` remains outside this request-time guard.
- GitHub reads reject custom pager settings from inherited or command-level environment and options, require a safe pager when terminal-creating wrappers are used, and refuse all browser-opening options. Trace destinations are checked against protected paths, and fetch checks use the selected remote's effective refspecs even when `--refmap` is supplied.
- Every workflow dispatch adds one shared system instruction that tells the model to leave GitHub writes and remote Git changes to LoopTroop, then continue local work after a refusal. OpenCode permission checks refuse direct GitHub writes, remote Git writes, writes to the original project checkout, and destructive changes to managed ticket worktrees, Git metadata, and LoopTroop state, including in-place edits, archive extraction and file sync destinations, and local Git operations that can overwrite managed state. Ordinary edits remain available in the assigned ticket worktree and local scratch repositories. Ordinary wrappers (including `script -- command`), inline shells, Git global options and aliases explicitly set by the command, `sed -f` script files, identity or root switching, Windows mutations, and symlink or home-path destinations receive the same checks. Local-path Git pushes are allowed only when effective Git configuration confirms that URL rewriting will not redirect the push remotely. Verified OpenCode v2 helper permission requests use the helper session and originating shell directory; pending requests cleared by a refusal do not abort the prompt. OpenCode v1 uses the session directory for relative shell paths because its permission events do not report each call's working directory. Broad saved OpenCode "always allow" rules can bypass this request-time guard. Writes to runtime setup and tool-cache paths remain available; the runtime root, execution logs, and approved setup profile stay protected. Refusals report the reason and leave the current workflow session running; LoopTroop's own Git and GitHub operations are unaffected. OpenCode helper sessions may have independent permissions. Aliases loaded from existing Git configuration, arbitrary shell scripts, custom clients, and network tools with existing credentials remain outside this check.

### Performance

- Keep Help downloads out of ticket questions, cache current documentation briefly, and reuse unchanged ticket evidence for up to one minute after checking its inputs. Evidence preparation has a separate deadline from the model answer. Ticket logs and workflow artifacts are collected within recorded limits so large histories cannot overwhelm a chat answer.
